summary: Independent expectations/execution pass preserves the separation between GEV company quality and entry attractiveness. Primary Q2 evidence supports unusually strong execution and raised guidance, while canonical methodology already flags substantially weaker valuation opportunity than operating quality. The appropriate execution stance remains disciplined rather than momentum-driven. XTND has no defensible opportunity state until capitalization/runway is normalized.

materialFindings.finding: GEV reported $24.2B Q2 orders (+88% organically), $176B backlog, 116 GW of gas backlog plus slot reservations, $5.1B Q2 free cash flow and $13.1B cash, and raised 2026 guidance. These are valid operating anchors for a base case.

Canonical GEV Earth Score is 81.8 with data confidence 92.4, but marketValuationOpportunity is only 56 versus financialOperatingMomentum 94.75 and alignment2036 95.5. This internal spread correctly signals that company truth and investment attractiveness must remain separate.

A defensible scenario bridge should anchor on disclosed capacity milestones (20 GW annual gas-turbine output in Q3 2026, 24 GW in 2028, actions toward 30 GW in 2030) and backlog conversion, while leaving terminal multiples, consensus precision and crowding unknown unless sourced contemporaneously.

unknowns: No authoritative contemporaneous consensus distribution was acquired in this pass; consensus divergence remains unknown.
No defensible contemporaneous crowding/positioning dataset was acquired; crowding remains unknown.
XTND valuation asymmetry cannot be calculated responsibly before basic/fully diluted capitalization and cash runway are reconciled.
